newsitem.title: USA: Continental pilots in the dark on merger.
newsitem.headline: Continental pilots in the dark on merger.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc pilots were left in the dark Wednesday as reports surfaced of talks between the Houston-based carrier and Delta Air Lines Inc, the head of the Houston airline's pilots union said.

"This was all news to the pilots," said Capt. Bob Wilson, president of the Independent Association of Continental Pilots, who planned to meet with company executives Wednesday afternoon to discuss reports Continental had initiated merger talks with Atlanta-based Delta.

Approval from the pilot's union was considered a key to completing the deal, and the fact that the union had not yet been consulted was seen as a sign that any talks -- if in fact talks were ongoing -- were still in the preliminary stages.
"You would be doing the numbers before you talk to any employee groups because it would increase the likelihood of a leak," said transportation analyst Timothy Ross of S.G. Warburg & Co.
In a memo to employees, Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune would not confirm or deny the merger talks, but said there was no merger on the immediate horizon.
Continental's pilots have had a bumpy relationship with the airline since former Chairman Frank Lorenzo put the airline into bankruptcy in 1983 and rescinded its labor agreements.

But the union inked a new labor pact with Continental in June 1995, and Wilson credits Bethune with reviving the once-ailing airline. "What he did was provide the environment for the employees to bring the airline back from the brink," he said.
